sentences: `M = M op DATA` on the 64-bit LDS element at `vaddr + offset` (two dwords, low first); the `_rtn_` form returns the old 64 bits in a VGPR pair.
A bitwise op works on each bit alone, so it is emitted as one 32-bit `OpAtomicAnd/Or/Xor` per dword.
That leaves exactly the memory a 64-bit atomic would, without Int64 atomics on Workgroup memory (optional in Vulkan).
**Approximation:** the returned pair comes from two reads, so another lane's 64-bit op on the same element between them can show up half done; the memory result is exact.
The other 64-bit LDS atomics (`add/sub/min/max_u64`, `wrxchg_b64`, `cmpst_b64`) carry between dwords or need the pair to move together, and still raise `Unsupported`.
Until 2026-11-22 these three were rejected as well.
CPU-checked by `tests/semantic/test_lds_bitwise_b64.py` (all six forms, offsets, `vdst` aliasing the data, seeded values).
Measured on native gfx1100 for all six forms, both dwords of each pair, with the returning forms giving the old pair.
